findings.description: none: Round-11 claim 1 holds at HEAD e7e299b8: `/work/submit` with `projection_key` and every `/work/reconcile` call `authorize_operation(..., operation="publish_work_projection", resource=<exact change_id>)` before `WorkQueueService` mutation (`coordination_api.py:1204-1228`, `1254-1268`). Dispatch, `--check-vendors`, and `--list-agents` all call that helper with `Path(args.cwd)`. `test_dispatch_preserves_sdk_only_coordinator_roster` and precedence tests passed.
findings.resolution: Shared resolver/cwd and SDK-only authority verified.

findings.description: Critical: Documented cosmetic reserved-label bounds are insufficient for projection availability. `/issues/create` accepts arbitrary labels with no `authorize_operation` and no reserved-label rejection (`coordination_api.py:1328-1348`, `issue_service.py:241-276`). An authenticated caller can insert an unowned issue labelled `change:<victim>` and `projection:autopilot-phase`; both labelled SQL paths then fail closed with `projection_key_collision` before any repair (`039_…sql:98-112`, `:226-240`), blocking legitimate publishers until an administrator deletes or otherwise clears the planted row. Ownership and heads remain unstolen, but elevated publication is denied.
findings.resolution: Reject or strip `projection:autopilot-phase` (and optionally the paired change label when that marker is present) on ordinary issue create/update APIs, or require an elevated operation before accepting reserved projection labels outside labelled work-queue RPCs.

findings.description: Critical: Ordinary issue APIs can mutate registry-owned projection rows. `/issues/update` replaces labels wholesale and `/issues/close` sets `status=completed` with no ownership or projection guard (`coordination_api.py` update/close handlers; `issue_service.py:424-425`, `480-493`). Knowing the canonical task UUID, any API-key principal can clear `projection:autopilot-phase` / `change:<id>` markers or close the board-visible row until the next labelled submit/reconcile restores owned state. This exceeds the documented “cosmetic only / cannot obtain ownership or advance heads” bound for board and SSE integrity.
findings.resolution: Refuse label/status mutations on rows present in `work_queue_projection_ownership` from ordinary issue APIs, or require `publish_work_projection` (or an admin operation) before mutating owned projection issues.

findings.description: Optional: In-process Autopilot `converge()` still builds `ReviewOrchestrator.from_coordinator()` when `agents_yaml_path` is omitted (`convergence_loop.py:610-614`), bypassing `_orchestrator_for_dispatch` local-before-coordinator resolution keyed to `worktree_path`. Round-11 disposition claimed this construction did not exist; it does. This can revive the stale coordinator/global roster class outside the fixed CLI dispatcher.
findings.resolution: When `orchestrator` is None and `agents_yaml_path` is absent, resolve via `_orchestrator_for_dispatch(None, worktree_path)` (or equivalent explicit → reviewed-cwd-local → coordinator → disk chain, including SDK-only authority).

findings.description: FYI: Local MCP `db` transport still reaches `WorkQueueService.submit` / `reconcile_projection`, which authorize `submit_work` rather than `publish_work_projection` (`coordination_mcp.py:357-422`, `work_queue.py:777-780`, `907-910`). Autopilot’s bridge path uses HTTP and therefore hits the elevated gate; D12 relies on coordinator-only MCP and trust-level-3 local publishers. Mis-pointing local MCP at a trust-level-2 process identity would bypass the elevated operation name while still satisfying `submit_work`.
findings.resolution: Accepted under D12’s coordinator-only/TL3 local-publisher assumption; optionally align service-layer policy with `publish_work_projection` when a projection key/labels are present for defense in depth.

findings.description: FYI: With `POLICY_ENGINE=cedar`, `CedarPolicyEngine` defaults missing `context.trust_level` to 1 (`policy_engine.py:735`), and HTTP `authorize_operation` does not inject resolved trust. Live probe: Cedar deny without trust context, allow with `trust_level=3`. Default `native` engine resolves trust and correctly permits TL3 / denies TL2 for `publish_work_projection`. Spec D12 requires native/profile retention, which holds; Cedar HTTP publishers remain fail-closed unless callers pass trust.
findings.resolution: No change required for the default native path; if Cedar is a supported production mode, resolve and inject trust in `authorize_operation` or inside `CedarPolicyEngine` as Native does.

findings.description: none: Coordinator-free isolation remains intact: `QueueProjectionAdapter` is constructed only for coordinated hosts; isolation tests fail closed if `try_submit_work` / `try_reconcile_work_projection` / label helpers are imported or called from free tiers (`test_phase_projection_isolation.py`). Spec D10 scenario satisfied.
